{{nihongo|'''Soganimasu Sogatsuhiko Shrine'''|宗我坐宗我都比古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine''' (そがにますそがつひこじんじゃ<ref>[http://www.narashinsei.com/search/%E3%82%B5%E8%A1%8C/%E5%AE%97%E6%88%91%E5%9D%90%E5%AE%97%E6%88%91%E9%83%BD%E6%AF%94%E5%8F%A4%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine] (Nara Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines).</ref>/そがにいますそがつひこじんじや{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}/そがのそがつひこじんじゃ{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Soga-chō, {{ill|Kashihara, Nara|Q496319|qid=Q496319}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} (major shrine), and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine rank}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

It is also commonly known as “Iruka-no-miya.” The shrine is known as being associated with the ancient powerful clan, the {{ill|Soga clan|Q909854|qid=Q909854}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
The enshrined deities are the following two {{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}:
:* '''Sogatsuhiko-no-Kami''' (そがつひこのかみ, also written 宗我都比古神)
:* '''Sogatsuhime-no-Kami''' (そがつひめのかみ, also written 宗我都比売神)

In the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}} compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is listed as having two seats of deities. The entry records the name as “Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine,” meaning “the shrine that enshrines Sogatsuhiko in Soga (= Soga/Soga/Soga: a place name).” One of the two seats is identified as Sogatsuhiko-no-Kami, but the identity of the other seat is unclear.

Because the shrine name and deity name include “Sogatsuhiko,” the ritual practices of Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine are thought to be connected to the ancient powerful {{ill|Soga clan|Q909854|qid=Q909854}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}. Although the Soga clan is a well-known lineage, its original homeland ({{ill|Korean clans|Q846706|qid=Q846706}}) has not been definitively identified. Three main theories are known: that it was located in Soga (the area around present-day Soga-chō, Kashihara City) in {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} {{ill|Takaichi District, Nara|Q1117901|qid=Q1117901}} (the site of this shrine); that it was in {{ill|Katsujō district|Q11620858|qid=Q11620858}} of Yamato Province (around present-day {{ill|Gose, Nara|Q847334|qid=Q847334}}); or that it was in {{ill|Ishikawa district|Q11586399|qid=Q11586399}} (the eastern half of {{ill|Tondabayashi|Q490928|qid=Q490928}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}, and the {{ill|Minamikawachi District, Osaka|Q1347323|qid=Q1347323}} area){{Sfn|Soga clan (ancient clans)|2010}}{{Sfn|Soga (encyclopedia of ancient clans)|2015}}. Among these, the first theory (this area) is considered particularly persuasive, based on the place name “Soga,” the presence of Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine, and a passage in the *Kishi Kachō* that states of {{ill|Soga no Ishikawa no Sukune|Q11625205|qid=Q11625205|lt=Soga Ishikawa no Sukune}}: “Residence: Soga village, Takaichi district, Yamato Province”{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}{{Sfn|Soga clan (ancient clans)|2010}}{{Sfn|Soga (encyclopedia of ancient clans)|2015}}.

As mentioned above, the *Engishiki* Jinmyōchō lists two seats of deities. Regarding this, the *Gogun Jinjaki* assigns them to {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}} and {{ill|Soga no Ishikawa no Sukune|Q11625205|qid=Q11625205|lt=Ishikawa no Sukune}}, while shrine records from around the {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} era ({{ill|1688|Q7671|qid=Q7671}}–{{ill|1704|Q6824|qid=Q6824}}) assign them to {{ill|Hikofutsuoshi no Makoto no Mikoto|Q11487911|qid=Q11487911}} and Ishikawa no Sukune{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. In all cases, these figures are regarded as distant ancestors of the Soga clan. In contrast, the present practice enshrines the two deities Sogatsuhiko and Sogatsuhime, with their two wooden statues worshipped as the {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. In the Jinmyōchō, many shrines list two seats with the pattern “place name + tsu + hiko/hime,” and in the case of Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine as well, it is considered appropriate to view the enshrined deities as the two local tutelary gods Sogatsuhiko and Sogatsuhime{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1982}}.

== History ==
[[File:Sogatsuhiko-jinja, honden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main sanctuary}}]]
== Founding ==
The date of founding is unknown. According to the *Gogun Jinjaki*, during the reign of {{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}} (r. {{ill|593|Q33889|qid=Q33889}}–{{ill|628|Q30592|qid=Q30592}}), {{ill|Soga no Umako|Q1191233|qid=Q1191233}} built a shrine in Soga village to enshrine {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}} and {{ill|Soga no Ishikawa no Sukune|Q11625205|qid=Q11625205|lt=Ishikawa no Sukune}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}. On the other hand, shrine tradition holds that {{ill|Empress Jitō|Q232026|qid=Q232026}} (r. {{ill|690|Q23472|qid=Q23472}}–{{ill|697|Q23489|qid=Q23489}}), lamenting the downfall of the Soga clan, allowed Tokunaga Naigu, the second son of {{ill|Soga no Kurayamada no Ishikawa no Maro|Q3488899|qid=Q3488899}}, to succeed the {{ill|Ki clan|Q11605075|qid=Q11605075}}, and granted land to Naigu’s son Nagasue so that he might enshrine the ancestral deities and carry out shrine duties and cultivation; this event is regarded as the founding of the shrine{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}.

It is also known that the area around Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine encompasses the Nakazoshi site, an archaeological site with remains from the {{ill|Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858}} through the early {{ill|Kofun period|af|Kofun-tydperk|ar|فترة كوفون|az|Kofun dövrü|be|Кафун|bg|Кофун|bn|কোফুন যুগ|ca|Període Kofun|cs|Období Kofun|de|Kofun-Zeit|eo|Kofun-epoko|es|Período Kofun|eu|Kofun aroa|fa|دوره کوفون|fi|Kofun-kausi|fr|Période Kofun|he|תקופת קופון|hr|Razdoblje Kofun|hu|Kofun-kor|id|Zaman Kofun|it|Periodo Kofun|ja|古墳時代|ko|고훈 시대|lt|Kofun laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Kofun|nl|Kofunperiode|pl|Kofun (okres)|pt|Período Kofun|ro|Perioada Kofun|ru|Период Кофун|sh|Kofunski period|simple|Kofun period|sk|Obdobie Kofun|sl|Obdobje Kofun|sr|Кофун период|sv|Kofunperioden|th|ยุคโคฟุง|tl|Panahong Kofun|tr|Kofun Dönemi|uk|Період Кофун|vi|Thời kỳ Kofun|wuu|古坟时代|zh|古坟时代|zh_min_nan|Kohun sî-tāi|zh_yue|古墳時代|qid=Q459939}}, and many artifacts have been unearthed in and around the shrine grounds<ref>[http://www.city.kashihara.nara.jp/kankou/own_bunkazai/bunkazai/spot/nakazoshi.html Nakazoshi Site] (Kashihara City website “Kashihara Exploration Guide”).</ref><ref>“Nakazoshi Site,” *Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture*, Heibonsha, 1981.</ref>.

== Overview ==
According to a document from {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} 1 ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}}) in the *{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}*, the “Soga deity” at that time was assigned three households from {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} as {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|Q11589711|qid=Q11589711}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. Based on this record, there is also a theory that one of the 39 shrines in Yamato Province listed as having shrine households in the *Ōyamato no kuni shōzeichō* of {{ill|Tenpyō|br|Tenpyō|ca|Era Tenpyō|de|Tempyō|es|Tenpyō|fa|تنپیو|fr|Ère Tenpyō|ia|Tenpyo|id|Tempyō|it|Tenpyō|ja|天平|ko|덴표|no|Tenpyō|pt|Tenpyō|ru|Тэмпё|simple|Tenpyō|sr|Тенпјо|tr|Tenpyō|uk|Темпьо (ненґо)|zh|天平 (日本)|zh_yue|天平 (日本)|qid=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyō}} 2 ({{ill|730|Q23563|qid=Q23563}}) corresponds to this shrine{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}.

In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168}}, there are records of Sogatsuhiko-no-Kami being promoted in rank to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper, in {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten’an}} 3 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), and to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower, in {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 6 ({{ill|864|Q25041|qid=Q25041}}){{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}.

In the *Engishiki* Jinmyōchō compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is listed in Takaichi District, Yamato Province, as “Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine, two seats, both major; receiving offerings at the Tsukinami and Niiname festivals,” indicating that its two seats were ranked as a {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|Q134917288|qid=Q134917288}} and that it received offerings from the court at the {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}.

According to the *Yamato-shi*, during the {{ill|Early modern period|an|Edat Moderna|ar|الحقبة الحديثة المبكرة|ast|Edá Moderna|az|Erkən modern dövr|bar|Friae Neizeid|be|Ранні Новы час|bn|প্রারম্ভিক আধুনিক যুগ|br|Amzerioù modern|ca|Edat moderna|cs|Raný novověk|cy|Cyfnod Modern Cynnar|da|Tidlig moderne tid|de|Frühe Neuzeit|el|Πρώιμη νεότερη περίοδος|eo|Frua moderna epoko|es|Edad Moderna|et|Varauusaeg|eu|Aro Modernoa|fa|دوران نوین آغازین|fi|Varhaismoderni|fr|Époque moderne|gl|Idade Moderna|gn|Ára Ko'ãgagua|he|העת החדשה המוקדמת|hi|प्रारंभिक आधुनिक काल|hu|Korai újkor|ia|Etate Moderne|id|Periode modern awal|io|Modern-epoko|it|Età moderna|ja|近世|kbp|Alɩwaatʊ kɩfatʊ (Période moderne)|ko|근세|ku|Destpêka Dema Nûjen|kw|Oos Arnowydh A-Varr|lb|Neizäit|lfn|Eda moderna|li|Vreugmodernen Tied|lij|Etæ Modèrna|lld|Storia moderna|lmo|Età Modèrna|lo|ຍຸກ​ສະ​ໄຫມ​ຕົ້ນ​|lt|Naujieji amžiai|lv|Agrīnie jaunie laiki|mg|Andro Vaovao|mk|Ран нов век|new|प्रारम्भिक आधुनिक काल|nl|Vroegmoderne tijd|nn|Tidleg nytid|no|Tidlig moderne tid|oc|Edat Modèrna|pap|Edad Moderno|pcd|Histoère modérne|pl|Nowożytność|ps|لومړۍ معاصره دوره|pt|Idade Moderna|rm|Temp modern tempriv|ro|Epoca modernă timpurie|ru|Раннее Новое время|sc|Edade moderna|sh|Rani novi vijek|simple|Early modern period|sq|Periudha e hershme moderne|sr|Rani novi vek|stq|Eermodärne Tied|sv|Tidigmoderna tiden|th|สมัยใหม่ตอนต้น|tl|Makabagong kasaysayan|tr|Yeni Çağ|tt|Иртә яңа заман|uk|Ранній новий період|vi|Thời kỳ cận đại|vls|Nieuwn tyd|wuu|近世|yi|נייע צייט|zh|近世|zh_yue|近代史|qid=Q5308718}} it was known as “Iruka-no-miya”{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine (Kami-gami)|2000}}.

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in September {{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 40), it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}{{Sfn|Soga-ni-masu Sogatsuhiko Shrine Two Seats (Shikinaisha)|1982}}.
